steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Design brief: a concise statement of the problem to be solved - identifies the user, the need and the context. Not a solution - a starting point.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Design specification: a list of measurable criteria the product must meet - function, target user, dimensions, materials, cost, safety, aesthetics, environmental impact. Must be testable.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: User research: interviews, questionnaires, observation, focus groups - reveals real needs, not assumptions. Ask open questions, observe users in context, identify pain points.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Market research: analyse competing products - features, price points, materials, strengths, weaknesses. Identify gaps in the market and opportunities for innovation.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: A design brief states the PROBLEM, not the solution - 'design a storage device' not 'design a shelf' Specification points must be MEASURABLE - include numbers, sizes, weights, costs Always link research methods to the specific information they will reveal
